# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | FORMULA-SINK | 37378, 37456, 45635, 53383, 53647, 55979, 7902, 8942, 9569 | Agent writes Excel formulas into cells; grader reads them as empty. | OUTPUT-CONTRACT | contract: "write literal values" |
| 2 | TYPE-MISMATCH | 416-15, 54144, 56563 | Agent writes strings (e.g. date strings) where datetime/float/int expected. | OUTPUT-CONTRACT | contract: "use real typed values" |
| 3 | OVER-MODIFICATION | 38462, 39046, 416-15, 463-17, 48527, 59196, 59595 | Agent modifies cells outside the required logic or changes values that should be left alone. | BEHAVIORAL | rule: "leave untouched what is not asked" |
| 4 | VALUE-MISMATCH | 227-40, 267-18, 43436, 46897, 51-12, 80-42 | Calculation or selection logic is incorrect (too high/low/wrong values). | KNOWLEDGE/CAPABILITY | refined instructions on verification |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit — aim for MULTIPLE classes, incl. a NEW tool when a cluster needs one)
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FORMULA-SINK | CONTRACT | guidance.md | Explicit rule to compute results in Python and write literal values, never formulas. | Yes, passing tasks already do this. |
| TYPE-MISMATCH | CONTRACT | guidance.md | Explicit rule to write real typed values (datetime, float, int) instead of strings. | Yes, passing tasks already do this. |
| OVER-MODIFICATION | BEHAVIORAL | guidance.md | Explicit rule to only modify cells required by the instruction; leave others untouched. | Yes, passing tasks follow this. |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change: the trace it targets → what the guard/computation/new-tool now does on those exact inputs)
- 37378, 37456: wrote formula `=IF(...)` → now computes value in Python and writes literal.
- 416-15: wrote date as string `strftime('%m/%d/%Y')` → now writes as datetime object.
- 38462, 39046: changed cells that should be original input → now only modifies target range.

## Process & features used
- Serial analysis of trajectories.
- Used `analyze_trajectories.py` and custom scripts to extract code from trajectories.
- Prior iterations: none (this is iteration 1).

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- The rule against formulas is critical for this grader.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why — already-passing / needs gold / infra noise)
- Value-mismatch (Rank 4) skipped for now as it requires deeper task-specific analysis; focusing on structural/contract fixes first.
